snp5.5:2.4: For more on what “acquisition” (upadhi) means, see Sn 3:12, note 2.
snp5.5:3.4: This verse repeats, word for word, the second set of verses at Sn 3:12.
snp5.5:7.3: Nd II offers six valid readings of “above, below, across, in between”: (a) above = the future, below = the past, across/in between = the present; (b) above = the deva world, below = hell, across/in between = the human world; (c) above = skillfulness, below = unskillfulness, across/in between = indeterminate qualities; (d) above = the formless property, below = the property of sensuality, across/in between = the property of form; (e) above = pleasant feeling, below = painful feeling, across/in between = neither-pleasant-nor-painful feeling; (f) above = the body from the feet up, below = the body from the crown down, across/in between = the middle of the body.
snp5.5:7.5: On consciousness not becoming established, see SN 12:38, SN 12:63–64, SN 22:53–54, and SN 22:87, as well as the discussion in The Paradox of Becoming, chapter 7.
snp5.5:12.2: Becoming and non-becoming (or dis-becoming) are the two subtlest objects of craving that keep the round of birth and death going. See Ud 3:10, Iti 49, and MN 49, note 10, as well as The Paradox of Becoming.
